lessons.title: Pipes, fittings and preparing to lay
lessons.html:
Pipes and fittings

Irrigation systems carry water from the source (borehole, municipal supply, tank or dam) through a main line, valves and lateral lines to sprinklers or drippers. Your job is to lay these pipes in the trench and join them so they do not leak.

Common pipe types

PipeUseHow it is joined
PVC (rigid, usually grey or white)Main lines and laterals under pressureSolvent cement (glue) or rubber ring joints
HDPE (black, stiff poly pipe)Main and supply linesCompression fittings or welding by trained people
LDPE (black, soft poly pipe)Laterals, drip linesInsert or barbed fittings with clamps, or compression fittings

Pipes come in different sizes (diameter, in mm) and pressure classes. Use exactly the size and class shown on the plan. A smaller or weaker pipe can burst or give poor water flow.

Fittings

  • Couplings join two pipes in a line.
  • Elbows turn a corner.
  • Tees make a branch.
  • Reducers join a bigger pipe to a smaller pipe.
  • End caps close the end of a line.
  • Risers bring water up from the pipe to a sprinkler.

Before laying

  1. Check that the trench is the right depth, the bottom is even and free of stones and roots.
  2. Check the materials against the plan and the materials list: pipe sizes, fittings, quantities.
  3. Inspect pipes for cracks, dents or scratches. Do not use damaged pipe.
  4. Keep pipes in the shade until used. PVC becomes brittle and poly pipe gets soft and expands in strong sun.
  5. Keep pipe ends closed with tape or caps so soil, insects and frogs do not get inside.

lessons.title: Laying and joining pipes
lessons.html:
Laying and joining pipes

Laying

  • Lay the pipe on a bed of fine soil or sand on the trench floor.
  • Lay it loosely in a gentle snake shape, especially poly pipe on a hot day. Pipe shrinks when it cools and can pull out of fittings if laid tight.
  • Keep the pipe in the middle of the trench, away from sharp stones and the sides.
  • Do not drag pipes over rough ground or paving.

Cutting pipe

  • Cut straight and square with a pipe cutter or a fine-tooth saw.
  • Remove burrs (rough edges) inside and outside with a knife or file.
  • Measure twice, cut once.

PVC solvent joints

  1. Check the pipe and fitting are clean and dry.
  2. Test fit: the pipe should go part way into the fitting.
  3. Clean both surfaces with the cleaner your site uses.
  4. Apply solvent cement evenly to the pipe end and inside the fitting, as the tin says.
  5. Push the pipe fully into the fitting with a slight twist and hold for the time on the tin.
  6. Wipe off extra cement.
  7. Do not move or pressure the joint until it has cured for the time on the tin.

Solvent cement and cleaner are flammable and give off fumes. Use them in fresh air, keep away from flames, wear gloves and close the tin after use.

Compression and insert fittings

  • Loosen the nut, push the pipe fully in to the stop, then tighten by hand and finish as instructed. Do not over-tighten.
  • For insert fittings, push the pipe fully over the barb and tighten the clamp.

Valves and risers

Install valves in valve boxes so they can be reached later. Fit risers at the positions on the plan, upright and at the right height.

lessons.title: Flushing, testing and recording
lessons.html:
Flushing, testing and recording

Flushing

Before sprinklers or drippers are fitted, the pipes must be flushed. Dirt, sand and bits of pipe left inside will block nozzles and drippers.

  1. Leave the ends of lateral lines open, or remove end caps.
  2. Open the water slowly.
  3. Let water run until it comes out clean.
  4. Close the ends and fit sprinklers or drippers.

Pressure testing

The system is tested before the trench is filled, so leaks can be found and fixed easily.

  • Keep all joints uncovered.
  • Your supervisor will fill the system and bring it to the test pressure for the time set in the specification.
  • Walk the whole line and look for drips, wet soil and spraying joints.
  • Mark any leak. Release the pressure, fix it, and test again.
  • Only backfill when the supervisor says the test has passed.

Never stand over a joint or end cap when the system is being pressurised. A fitting can blow off with force.

Recording

  • Mark changes from the plan on the drawing (an as-built plan): where pipes and valves really are.
  • Measure valve positions from fixed points such as walls or corners.
  • Give the drawing to your supervisor. It helps whoever repairs the system later.

Cleaning up

  • Collect pipe off-cuts, packaging and empty tins. Dispose of solvent tins as your site says.
  • Return tools and left-over fittings to the store and record them.

Key points

  • Use the pipe type, size and class shown on the plan.
  • Inspect pipes, keep them shaded and keep ends closed.
  • Lay pipe loosely on a stone-free bed and cut square, removing burrs.
  • Follow the solvent cement instructions and let joints cure.
  • Flush, pressure test and fix leaks before backfilling, and record as-built positions.
